lessons.title: Making an offer
objectives: Make a practical offer and respond clearly.
Use a main idea and one relevant detail in a response about offering help at an event.

content_sections.title: Notice form and meaning (8 minutes)
content_sections.body: Read the model aloud twice: 'Can I bring some drinks for the meeting on Saturday?' Underline the words that show the situation, time, or result. In this lesson, make a practical offer and respond clearly. Keep the language connected: do not give isolated words.

content_sections.title: Guided dialogue (8 minutes)
content_sections.body: Partner A begins a realistic exchange about offering help at an event. Partner B asks for one missing detail. Swap roles and make one change to the time, place, reason, quantity, or next action. Check that the exchange achieves: Make a practical offer and respond clearly.

content_sections.title: Independent response (6 minutes)
content_sections.body: Create a short message about offering help at an event without reading the model. Include a main event or plan and one precise detail. Speak it once slowly, then once at a natural pace. Listen for whether the key information is clear.

exercises.prompt: Choose the response that gives a clear, useful message for this situation: offering help at an event.
options: Can I bring some drinks for the meeting on Saturday?
Would you like to join our park clean-up and bring a pair of gloves?
My card did not work at the machine, so I asked a staff member for help.
exercises.correct_answer: Can I bring some drinks for the meeting on Saturday?

exercises.prompt: Complete the model with the missing words: 'Can I bring some drinks for the ____?'
Read this short message for the lesson 'Making an offer' and identify the real-life situation it describes.
exercises.stimulus: Can I bring some drinks for the meeting on Saturday? The message gives one main point and one detail for the listener.

questions.question: What situation does the message describe?
acceptable_answers: The message is about offering help at an event.

exercises.prompt: Speak for 30–45 seconds about offering help at an event. State the main message, add a relevant detail, and answer one follow-up question.

criteria: Communicates the main message about offering help at an event clearly.
Adds a relevant detail and responds appropriately to a follow-up question.

listening.instruction: Listen once to a short message about offering help at an event. Answer the question before the transcript is revealed, then listen again and check the key detail.
listening.goal: Identify the situation and a useful detail in a short message about offering help at an event.
listening.transcript: Can I bring some drinks for the meeting on Saturday?
listening.question: What is the message mainly about?
listening.answer: The listener should understand that it concerns offering help at an event.
constraints: Keep the transcript private before the learner answers the first question.
Use only the supplied transcript; do not require media.

speaking.instruction: Roleplay offering help at an event. Learner role: explain the situation and give one useful detail. Tutor role: be a helpful listener, ask one specific follow-up, and confirm the next step. Begin with a natural greeting and finish once both roles agree on the next action.
speaking.goal: Complete a clear, practical exchange about offering help at an event.
constraints: Name the learner and tutor roles before the first turn.
Use at most three tutor turns and stop after the agreed next step.

pronunciation.instruction: Say the model for offering help at an event in two thought groups. Mark the pause between ideas, then stress the word that gives the key action, time, quantity, reason, or request. Record a second attempt after listening to your first attempt.
pronunciation.goal: Make the key information in offering help at an event easy to hear.
pronunciation.target: Thought-group pause and key-word stress in making an offer
constraints: Assess pronunciation only when learner audio is supplied.
Return NOT_ASSESSED when learner audio is unavailable.

writing.instruction: Write a 35–50 word message about offering help at an event. Include the main event or plan, one precise detail, and the next action or response. Submit your own draft before requesting feedback.
writing.goal: Write a connected, useful short message about offering help at an event.
constraints: Wait for the learner draft before giving feedback.
Give concise feedback only; do not replace the learner draft.

content_sections.title: Recall and select (8 minutes)
content_sections.body: Work without notes first. For the situation 'reviewing arrangements', say one sentence that meets this goal: Review offers, invitations, arrangements, and changes. Then check the model: 'I can make an offer, arrange details, and explain a change politely.' Identify one word or phrase that makes the message clear.

content_sections.title: Compare two responses (8 minutes)
content_sections.body: Give one clear response for reviewing arrangements, then ask a partner one follow-up question. Compare the response with the model and repair one missing time, reason, place, quantity, or next step. Use the whole unit's familiar language rather than memorising one sentence.

content_sections.title: Self-check and transfer (6 minutes)
